# Generated and binary files

Files that are produced by a tool, or that have no comment syntax, and are
therefore documented here rather than annotated in place. Editing any of
them is either pointless (the next build overwrites it) or impossible (the
format has no comments).

---

## `frontend/dist/` — production build output

**Generated by:** `npm run build` in `frontend/`, which runs `vite build`.

**Committed?** No. `dist/` is in the root `.gitignore`. The copy on disk is
whatever was built last; Vercel builds its own on deploy and never uses this
one.

**Safe to edit?** No. Every file here is overwritten on the next build, and
the JavaScript is minified — a change would be lost and unreadable in the
meantime.

**Regenerate with:** `cd frontend && npm run build`

### Contents

| File | Size | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | 403 B | The SPA shell. Built from `frontend/index.html` with the fingerprinted script and stylesheet tags injected. |
| `assets/index-*.js` | ~1.9 MB | The whole application: React, React Router, all pages, components, hooks and services, minified into one chunk. This is the bundle the chunk-size warning refers to. |
| `assets/index-*.css` | ~38 KB | Every stylesheet from `src/styles/` concatenated and minified. |
| `assets/html2canvas-*.js` | ~200 KB | `html2canvas`, pulled in transitively by `jspdf` for rendering DOM to an image during PDF export. Split into its own chunk because it is large and only needed when exporting. |
| `assets/index.es-*.js` | ~151 KB | The ES-module build of `jspdf`. |
| `assets/purify.es-*.js` | ~27 KB | `DOMPurify`, a `jspdf` dependency used to sanitise HTML before it is drawn into a PDF. |
| `favicon.svg`, `icons.svg` | — | Copied verbatim from `frontend/public/`. |

### Why the filenames have hashes

`index-BBww2N4a.js` — the `BBww2N4a` is a hash of the file's contents. Change
the source, and the name changes. That is what lets `vercel.json` cache
everything under `/assets/` for a year with `immutable`, while `index.html`
is never cached: the HTML is what points at the current hashes, so it must
always be fetched fresh.

### Reading a minified bundle

If you ever need to, `vite build` can emit source maps:

```
# vite.config.js
build: { sourcemap: true }
```

They are off here, which is the usual choice for production — a source map
publishes the original source.

## `.DS_Store` files (13)

macOS Finder metadata: window position, icon arrangement, view settings.
Binary, of no use to anyone else, and written automatically by Finder into
every directory it browses.

They are covered by `.gitignore`, but **thirteen are still tracked** because
they were committed before that rule existed. Ignoring a file does not
untrack one already in the index.

To remove them from version control while keeping them on disk:

```bash
git rm --cached '*.DS_Store'
git commit -m "Untrack .DS_Store files"
```

Tracked locations: repository root, `backend/`, `backend/database/`,
`backend/modules/`, `backend/modules/payments/`, `backend/modules/workers/`,
`frontend/`, `frontend/src/`, `frontend/src/components/`,
`frontend/src/components/export/`, `frontend/src/components/finance/`,
`frontend/src/components/payments/`, `frontend/src/styles/`.

## SVG assets

SVG is XML and does accept `<!-- -->` comments, so these two are annotated in
place rather than here.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `frontend/public/favicon.svg` | Browser tab icon. Files in `public/` are copied to `dist/` untouched and served from the site root — referenced as `/favicon.svg`, never imported. |
| `frontend/public/icons.svg` | An SVG sprite sheet: several icons in one file, each wrapped in a `<symbol>` with an id, referenced elsewhere via `<use href="/icons.svg#name">`. One request instead of one per icon. |

Their copies in `frontend/dist/` are build output — do not edit those.

## `backend/database/snapshots/schema-production.sql`

Not generated by a build, but produced by `pg_dump` rather than hand-written.
It is a point-in-time record of the deployed schema, kept for comparison when
a migration behaves unexpectedly. It is **not** part of the migration chain
and must not be run to set a database up — use `002_baseline_supabase.sql`
for that.

Regenerate with:

```bash
pg_dump "$DATABASE_URL" --schema-only --no-owner --no-privileges \
  > backend/database/snapshots/schema-production.sql
```
